Bloomberg reports that Apple is pushing for the launch of an iPad mini with an OLED display before October this year, and has revealed the expected update timeline for the entry-level iPad, iPad Air, and iPad Pro. Details below.

"The biggest iPad mini revamp in half a century"

Although rumors of the next iPad mini adopting an OLED display have been circulating for some time, Bloomberg has now provided a more precise launch timeline.

According to the latest report, "Apple is preparing to release a new OLED iPad mini (internal codename J510) as early as this fall, with plans to begin sales in October." The report also noted that Apple "is developing an OLED upgrade for the iPad Air," but "has no current plans to put OLED in the entry-level iPad and will continue using cheaper LCD screens in the near term."

Earlier this week, Weibo tipster yeux1122 also said the iPad mini would adopt an OLED screen, but claimed the device would not feature ProMotion technology, with the refresh rate staying fixed at 60Hz.

Returning to the Bloomberg report, it noted that adding OLED technology could push the iPad mini's price even higher. The device currently starts at $599, up from $499 before Apple raised pricing across most of its product lines a few weeks ago.

The report also shared Apple's expected timeline for the rest of the iPad lineup:

According to people familiar with the matter, a new entry-level iPad with the internal codename J581 is expected to launch as early as the first quarter of next year. The main change is a processor upgrade rather than a major design overhaul. The new iPad Air will continue to come in 11-inch and 13-inch sizes. New models with internal codenames J807 and J837 are expected to debut in spring. Apple also plans to release new iPad Pro models around the same time, as Bloomberg reported last month.

Finally, Bloomberg reiterated a report from a few days ago that Apple is expected to update the Apple Pencil next year, with the new model potentially featuring a replaceable battery design.
